title: JEE Main 2026 (April 4th, Shift 1) - Mathematics - Differential Equations
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = (1 + x + x^2)(1 - y + y^2)$, $y(0) = \frac{1}{2}$. Then $(2y(1) - 1)$ is equal to:
questions.explain:
Using separation of variables:
$\int \frac{dy}{y^2 - y + 1} = \int (x^2 + x + 1) dx$
$\int \frac{dy}{(y - 1/2)^2 + 3/4} = \frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{x^2}{2} + x + C$
Integrating the left side gives:
$\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{y - 1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2} \right) = \frac{x^3}{3} + \frac{x^2}{2} + x + C \implies \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{2y - 1}{\sqrt{3}} \right) = \frac{2x^3 + 3x^2 + 6x}{6} + C$
Substitute the initial condition $y(0) = \frac{1}{2}$ to find $C$:
$\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \tan^{-1}(0) = 0 + C \implies C = 0$.
Now calculate for $x = 1$:
$\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{2y(1) - 1}{\sqrt{3}} \right) = \frac{2(1) + 3(1) + 6(1)}{6} = \frac{11}{6}$.
$\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{2y(1) - 1}{\sqrt{3}} \right) = \frac{11\sqrt{3}}{12}$.
Solving for $(2y(1) - 1)$:
$2y(1) - 1 = \sqrt{3} \tan \left( \frac{11\sqrt{3}}{12} \right)$.
